# Trade desk rulebook (season 2026)

This rulebook is the only authority in this league. Real NBA rules do not apply.

**R1. Salary cap.** The salary cap is $155M. A team may sign a free agent only if its payroll after the signing is at or below the cap, unless the signing uses the minimum exception (R6).

**R2. Trade salary matching.** In a trade, if a team's payroll after the trade is above the cap, the salary it takes in must be no more than 125% of the salary it sends out plus $0.1M. Draft picks carry no salary.

**R3. Hard apron.** The hard apron is $196M. No transaction may take a team's payroll above the apron. A team that is already above the apron may only make transactions that reduce its payroll.

**R4. Roster limits.** No transaction may leave a team with more than 15 players. A team must finish the day with at least 13 players.

**R5. Trade restriction.** A player whose contract carries a no-trade clause or an active trade restriction cannot be included in any trade.

**R6. Minimum exception.** A team over the cap may sign a free agent for exactly $2.3M if it has an open roster spot. The player must accept: a free agent asking more than $2.3M declines a minimum offer.

**R7. Waivers.** Waiving a player removes him from the roster immediately. If his contract is guaranteed, his salary for this season stays on the team's payroll as dead money. Non-guaranteed salary is cleared. A waiver cannot be undone.

**R8. Luxury tax.** The luxury tax line is $188M. Payroll above the line is taxed. The tax line is not a hard limit; only the apron (R3) is.

**R9. Draft picks.** Draft picks may be traded. A team may not trade away its own first-round picks for two consecutive years; it must keep at least one of them.

**R10. Trade structure.** A trade involves exactly two teams. Every asset a team sends must be owned by that team at the time of the trade. Executed trades are final.

Signed C Oscar Tshiebwe (rating 62, career 60) to a one-year minimum deal at $2.3M. He was the only free-agent center at or above the 60 bar, and he was asking exactly the minimum, so the minimum exception (R6) covered it with no cap gymnastics and no assets out the door. Production backs the rating: 7.8 pts / 6.6 reb in 16.6 min this season, 63.4% FG, 20.3 PER - a real rebounding backup for Bam, not a body.

I worked the trade market first and it was a dead end at a sensible price. Cheap quality centers exist (Queta 70 at $2.35M in BOS, Landale 65 at $2.3M in ATL, Sims 64 at $2.46M in MIL, Ware 67 at $4.44M in MIL), but every offer built around Jahmir Young, Dru Smith, or Nikola Jovic plus one or two second-rounders was declined as too light. If you want more apron room back before the deadline, Simone Fontecchio ($8.31M, rating 58, expiring) is the obvious salary to move, and the roster is now full, so any further addition requires a trade or a waiver first.

steps.text:
Shed $6.62M by trading Dean Wade (F, value 60, $6.62M expiring) to Charlotte for no salary back. Payroll: $211.97M -> $205.35M; roster 15 -> 14, no dead money.

Why Wade: the top five by value (Mitchell 87, Harden 86, Mobley 80, Allen 75, Tyson 70) were off limits. Of the remaining players with a salary large enough to clear $5M on his own, Wade was both the cheapest and the lowest-rated (Merrill $8.48M/68, Schroder $14.1M/66, Strus $15.94M/65), so this was the least basketball value surrendered per dollar saved. No combination of the sub-$5M guys works: we can only shed two bodies before hitting the 13-man floor (R4), and the two cheapest pairs top out at $4.6M.

Legality: R3 bars any move that raises payroll for a team already over the $196M apron, so a pure salary dump was the only route; Charlotte sits $27.75M under the cap with an open spot, so R2 salary matching does not bind them. Waiving was a non-starter - every CLE contract is guaranteed, so R7 would have kept the money on the books as dead money. Trade was confirmed legal with no violations and accepted before execution.

Cap position now: $205.35M, $50.75M over the $154.6M cap, $17.45M over the $187.9M tax line, and $9.45M over the $196M hard apron. We are still apron-restricted, meaning every further transaction must reduce payroll and we cannot take back salary in any trade. I tried to attach a second-round pick as a sweetener in both Charlotte and Brooklyn versions of the deal; both declined to pay anything for Wade, so no assets came back and all four of our own picks are intact.

If you want out from under the apron, it takes $9.45M more. The clean version is Schroder ($14.1M) or Strus ($15.94M) to a cap-room team - Brooklyn and Charlotte both accepted a straight Strus dump when I tested it - which would also drop us under the tax line. That costs a rotation guard and leaves 13 players, so I did not do it without your say-so.

**R1. Salary cap.** The salary cap is $155M. A team may sign a free agent only if its payroll after the signing is at or below the cap, unless the signing uses the minimum exception (R6).

**R2. Trade salary matching.** In a trade, if a team's payroll after the trade is above the cap, the salary it takes in must be no more than 125% of the salary it sends out plus $0.1M. Draft picks carry no salary.

**R3. Hard apron.** The hard apron is $196M. No transaction may take a team's payroll above the apron. A team that is already above the apron may only make transactions that reduce its payroll.

**R4. Roster limits.** No transaction may leave a team with more than 15 players. A team must finish the day with at least 13 players.

**R5. Trade restriction.** A player whose contract carries a no-trade clause or an active trade restriction cannot be included in any trade.

**R6. Minimum exception.** A team over the cap may sign a free agent for exactly $2.3M if it has an open roster spot. The player must accept: a free agent asking more than $2.3M declines a minimum offer.

**R7. Waivers.** Waiving a player removes him from the roster immediately. If his contract is guaranteed, his salary for this season stays on the team's payroll as dead money. Non-guaranteed salary is cleared. A waiver cannot be undone.

**R8. Luxury tax.** The luxury tax line is $188M. Payroll above the line is taxed. The tax line is not a hard limit; only the apron (R3) is.

**R9. Draft picks.** Draft picks may be traded. A team may not trade away its own first-round picks for two consecutive years; it must keep at least one of them.

**R10. Trade structure.** A trade involves exactly two teams. Every asset a team sends must be owned by that team at the time of the trade. Executed trades are final.

Done: acquired F Kyshawn George (73 rated, $2.97M, 3 yrs) from Washington for G Ajay Mitchell (70, $3.0M) and our 2028 second-round pick.

Why this deal: there were no 70+ free-agent forwards, so a trade was the only route, and we had exactly one forward on the roster (Jaylin Williams, 61) against eleven guards. I shopped every 70+ forward in the $2-13M range - Coward (MEM), Marshall (DAL), Keegan Murray (SAC), Brandon Miller (CHA), Buzelis (CHI), Jaquez (MIL) - and every package built from our surplus mid-salary guards (Wiggins, Joe, Wallace, Kenrich, McCain, Topic) plus seconds was refused. Washington was the one partner whose price landed inside our range. I worked it down in stages: Mitchell alone was declined, Mitchell plus a 2028 first was accepted, and I kept trimming until they took Mitchell plus a single 2028 second - so we kept both first-rounders (2027, 2028) and the 2027 second.

Value: George is a 73-rated forward on essentially the same money and contract length as the 70-rated guard we gave up, and he fills the one hole on the roster rather than adding to the guard glut.

Cap position: payroll $184.38M (down $0.03M). Cap $154.6M, so $29.78M over the cap but $3.5M UNDER the $187.9M tax line - no tax bill - and $11.52M under the $195.9M hard apron. Roster is full at 15, no dead money. Picks remaining: 2027 1st, 2027 2nd, 2028 1st.
